# Secret and endpoint audit

**The inspected source, five service image identities, generated files and active synthetic credential/config volumes pass their bounded checks. Strict endpoint acceptance remains blocked for this capture because the running Kong instance still emits a production issuer hostname.** No unresolved secret-detector finding remained after reviewing explicitly synthetic fixture credentials, public identifiers and request metadata. This is not proof that every byte in every dependency, database page or historical log is free of real secrets.

Capture: 2026-09-05T12:07:38.500393+00:00 to 2026-09-05T12:07:44.652787+00:00. Machine evidence: [secret-and-endpoint-audit.pre-replay1.json](secret-and-endpoint-audit.pre-replay1.json). No raw configuration, credential values, tokens or application logs were written to this report. The audit did not start or restart containers, modify runtime volumes, send network probes, or run application workloads. Source/config edits described below are for the next boot.

## Production issuer finding and applied correction

The old Kong default at `ENV2_COMPOSE/substitutes/kong-lite/server.py` was `https://edge.razorpay.com`. No PASSPORT_ISS override existed in the inspected running container. `_mint_passport_jwt` places that value in the `iss` claim, and sampled Payouts logs record it at `context.passport.passport.iss`. This is effective identity configuration containing a production hostname and prevents an unqualified no-production-hostname statement.

The inspected path uses the issuer as an identity string; it does not dereference that URL. Pinned source evidence is Payouts `pkg/passport/handler.go:63–79`, `github.com/razorpay/goutils/passport/v3@v3.4.0/handler.go:52–80`, and `passport.go:27`. The effective `github.com/golang-jwt/jwt@v3.2.2+incompatible` dependency is pinned in Payouts `go.mod:126`; `claims.go:32–59` supplies the inherited standard time validation. The existing configured key identifier and RSA verification path support the local issuer configuration. Runtime acceptance of the changed configuration still requires the next fresh scenario.

As requested, Kong's source default and its explicit Compose environment now use `https://identity.arena.invalid`. Python compilation and rendered Compose validation passed. **No restart was performed by this audit.** The local issuer differs from production identity, which is an intentional safety/fidelity difference. The existing configured key identifier, generated signing key, RS256 signature and validity timestamps remain unchanged. Old candidate2 evidence is retained. New issuer acceptance must use logs and scenarios scoped after the next restart; old logs cannot be relabelled clean.

Redis also prints a public GitHub help URL in its startup overcommit warning. That is a diagnostic reference, not an effective service endpoint or observed outbound call. It is separately classified rather than silently discarded.

## Scanner interpretation

Raw scanner matches were not treated as confirmed secrets. Four generated-config matches were reviewed: two explicit arena-only placeholder Password fields traced to checked-in templates, and two occurrences of the Splitz `forDualWriteDirectPushToAPI` experiment identifier. Runtime GPG_KEY matches are public 40-hex signing-key fingerprints inherited unchanged from base-image metadata. Log UUID idempotency keys and 64-hex request hashes are request metadata, not authentication credentials. Their exact field/type classifications and source locations are retained in the JSON; values are not printed.

Known current generated secret values were compared in memory with configuration, environment and logs. An independent rerender and runtime-volume byte comparison establish consistency with the arena generation path. They cannot independently attest the historical randomness or origin of every input value. Public IFSC/bank-directory metadata, first-party source and third-party dependency code intentionally remain real reference inputs; “fully synthetic” applies to arena customer/merchant fixtures and locally generated credentials, not every bundled byte.

## Remaining limits

Full linked-binary/dependency scanning, exhaustive mutable datastore-volume inspection, earlier/rotated/future logs, application-file logs, and unused Mozart mock volume contents remain unverified. No heavy image export, database dump or full-volume scanner was run while acceptance was active. Neither entropy nor zero known-pattern findings proves absolute absence of real secrets. Complete strict endpoint acceptance requires the new issuer deployment and a fresh successful scenario/log capture.

The audit also removed trailing whitespace from the two API schema input files only. SQL meaning is unchanged. Existing generated provenance may retain the preceding DDL whitespace hash until the next regeneration.
